title: Investigating serial killing by CD8+ T cells using the novel "kiss-of-death" intercellular labeling platform
text:
This study investigates the mechanisms behind the serial killing behavior of cytotoxic T cells, a critical function
for effective anti-tumor immunity in cancer immunotherapy. We have developed a novel "kiss of death" assay
that directly labels T cells based on their cytolytic activity, enabling the identification of genes that regulate T cell-
mediated tumor cell killing through CRISPR screens. Our approach aims to uncover transcriptional, epigenetic,
and functional features of serial-killing T cells, ultimately providing insights to enhance T cell cytotoxicity within
the tumor microenvironment.

title: 2026 Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma Gordon Research Conference
text:
Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) is a major driver of nasopharyngeal carcinoma, a highly metastatic cancer that affects
people at relatively young ages. This conference will focus on roles of EBV, immune response, human genetics
and environmental factors that together cause this aggressive cancer. The 2026 Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma
Gordon Research Conference will bring together leading scientists, physician-scientists and trainees to
exchange recent advances, catalyze the development of new approaches and to expedite translation into the
clinic.

title: The evolutionary landscape of BRCA-associated breast cancer and its impact on endocrine therapy resistance
text:
Although most estrogen-driven breast cancers are initially sensitive to hormone therapy, 15–20% of patients do
not respond, and another 30–50% acquire resistance. There is accumulating evidence that estrogen signaling
and response to hormone therapy are affected by genetic alterations in tumors that lead to problems in
repairing DNA breaks that occur during cell division. This project aims to understand the mechanism by which
these genetic alterations, such as BRCA2 mutations, affects responsiveness to hormone therapy, which may
suggest new ways to overcome hormone therapy resistance by combination or sequence with other anticancer
drugs.

title: Innate immune memory for glioma immunotherapy
text:
Clinical trials of intratumor immunotherapies that stoke antitumor T cell function, e.g., virotherapy, have
shown encouraging early results in lethal WHO grade IV gliomas but are clearly not effective in most patients
treated to date. We discovered a decisive role for myeloid cells, which are derived from bone marrow resident
progenitors, in determining the anti-glioma efficacy of intratumor immunotherapy. This proposal will
mechanistically define effective virotherapy in patients with glioma, determine the role of bone marrow
progenitors in mediating glioma inflammation and responsiveness to immunotherapy, and will define a novel
strategy to engage antitumor functions of bone marrow progenitors.

title: Development of Innovative Resources to Advance MDS Research
text: Myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) is a heterogeneous group of progressive diseases of blood-forming hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells. Mechanisms of progression are poorly understood, and treatment options are limited. Our proposed highly collaborative and synergistic studies will produce a vibrant understanding of the path from molecular mutations to functional consequences in MDS and create a library of resources that can be shared with the greater MDS scientific community to enable further progress toward improved treatment strategies.

title: Mechanisms of Integrative and Conjugative Elements in Oral Bacteria
text:
Horizontal gene transfer through mobile genetic elements drives the adaptive evolution of bacterial pathogens
and contributes significantly to the spread of pathogenic properties throughout bacterial communities. We
recently discovered an integrative and conjugative element (a type of mobile element that is transferred from
cell to cell via conjugation) on the genome of the oral pathogen Streptococcus mutans. In this project, we will
investigate fundamental aspects of the element’s biology and its influence on S. mutans pathogenesis,
including the signals that govern this transfer, interactions with other mobile genetic elements and bacterial
defense systems, and elemental mechanisms that may ultimately harm the host bacterial cell.

title: Machine Learning for CCHD Screening using Dynamic Data
text:
Congenital heart disease is the most common birth defect and can be missed during pregnancy scan
and newborn exam leading to delayed detection, poor outcomes, and death. This application seeks to test and
develop a critical congenital heart disease screening machine learning algorithm that combines the current
screening standard, oxygen saturation, with additional features to assess blood flow and perfusion and
incorporates dynamic data from both inpatient and outpatient settings. This approach has the potential to
increase infant survival and will develop neonatal specific devices using artificial intelligence driven
diagnostics, which are priorities to the NICHD Pregnancy and Perinatology Branch and Obstetric and Pediatric
Pharmacology and Therapeutics Branch.

title: Neural Mechanisms of Immersive Virtual Reality in Chronic Pain
text:
This project examines, in chronic pain, the mechanisms of immersive virtual reality compared to the mechanisms
of placebo hypoalgesia. The potential of developing new non-pharmacological premises for low-risk interventions
for pain management is high.

title: Translational studies of cellular senescence as a regulator of doxorubicin-mediated arterial dysfunction
text:
Impaired artery function is a major risk factor for cardiovascular diseases in men and women who have
undergone cancer treatment with Doxorubicin chemotherapy. In the proposed project, I will investigate the role
of cellular senescence in regulating arterial dysfunction with Doxorubicin in preclinical mouse models and in
humans by conducting a trial in Doxorubicin-treated cancer patients. Overall, the findings of this project have
the potential to identify cellular senescence as a new therapeutic target for preventing/treating impaired artery
function with Doxorubicin and thereby reducing risk of cardiovascular diseases.

title: Novel pan-RAS Inhibitors from Natural Products: A Safer Approach for Colorectal Cancer Interception
text:
This project seeks to pioneer a novel therapeutic strategy aimed at preventing colorectal cancer in individuals
with precancerous polyps who are at high risk for progression to malignant disease by targeting the RAS
oncoprotein, a critical driver implicated in a significant portion of colorectal and other cancers. We will develop a
high-throughput screening assay to identify selective inhibitors of mutant RAS-expressing precancerous cells,
leveraging the NCI Natural Products Library, the world’s most extensive repository of bioactive natural
compounds. Promising candidates emerging from the screen will undergo comprehensive in vitro and in vivo
validation to assess their efficacy and potential for clinical translation, particularly in individuals with polyposis
syndromes.

title: Neural circuit mechanisms of dynamic learning rates
text:
We recently found that the orbitofrontal cortex (OFC) is required for animals to dynamically adjust their rate of
reinforcement learning based on uncertainty in the environment. This proposal will combine behavioral,
computational, circuit perturbation techniques and optical neuromodulatory sensors to determine whether OFC
neurons that project to a part of the brain called the ventral striatum control the rate of error-driven learning.
Neuropsychiatric disorders, including schizophrenia and bipolar disorder, are characterized by aberrant reward
processing and disordered decision-making, and a greater understanding of the circuit mechanisms of decision-
making could identify novel therapeutic targets for these disorders.

title: Investigating COUP-TFII in human vein development
text:
Knowledge of human blood vessel formation, including veins, is crucial for successfully vascularizing engineered
tissues in regenerative medicine and effectively treating organs affected by vascular diseases. However, the
processes guiding the development of human veins remain poorly understood due to the scarcity of samples
and the lack of relevant model systems. Here, I propose to study COUP-TFII, a transcription factor implicated in
venous differentiation in other species, and its mechanisms of action by leveraging a recently developed human
pluripotent stem cell differentiation protocol with the long-term goal of identifying new therapeutic pathways.

title: Complement in the Pathogenesis of Acute Chest Syndrome
text:
The proposed research is relevant to public health because sickle cell disease (SCD) is a life-threatening blood
disorder that affects millions of people worldwide, causing debilitating effects from acute painful episodes to
chronic organ dysfunction, limiting quality of life and expectancy. We have identified that complement activation
can drive acute chest syndrome (ACS), a major complication of SCD with high morbidity and mortality. In this
proposal, we will identify mechanisms and treatment options for ACS using a multi-faceted approach of animal
models, microfluidics and human samples to predict, prevent and treat ACS in SCD.

title: DMS/NIGMS 2: The mathematics of epigenetic regulation in human cells
text:
RELEVANCE (See instructions):
 This project can lead to theoretical and experimental advances that will enhance our understanding of
 epigenetic regulation in biological systems with broad implications in developmental biology and medicine.
 The proposed framework provides the flexibility to test new mathematical theory and experimental
 techniques, an aspect that transcends project specific objectives.

title: Human-Robot Collaboration in Construction: Assessing Cognitive Factors for Construction Workers Using Virtual Reality-Wearable Devices-Data Analytics Integrated Approach
text:
This project delves into the realm of Human-Robot Collaboration (HRC) within the construction
industry using Virtual Reality (VR) and wearable devices as tools, aiming to determine the impact
of levels of involving human-robot collaborations in construction on workers' (both male and
female) cognitive risk factors (including mental fatigue, attention, and stress) to enhance
occupational safety and health. Neglecting the understanding and analysis of cognitive risk factors
in HRC can lead to unforeseen safety hazards and health issues and further hinder the successful
adoption and efficiency of HRC in construction. At the completion of the proposed research, the
outcomes are expected to not only offer strong evidence to enhance safety measures and worker
well-being and promote effective HRC implementations, but also posit that the strategic
integration of robotics in construction tasks can foster a broader, more inclusive construction
working environment and alleviate workforce shortages, promoting the public well-being.

title: Prostate Cancer Program
text: Prostate Cancer Program: Summary/Abstract The overarching scientific goal of the HDFCCC Prostate Cancer (PR) Program is to use a team approach to advance the understanding of tumor biology and drive translation into more effective and targeted treatment. This is done through translational research spanning discovery bench science to clinical application and back. The PR Program also seeks to specifically address the burden of prostate cancer and disparities in outcomes among patients within the catchment area. The result will be a reduction the morbidity and mortality associated with prostate cancer and its treatments by leveraging a deep understanding of the disease at the biologic, clinical, and population levels. The PR Program approaches this mission with transdisciplinary research that is richly collaborative and translational, organized around three specific aims: (1) to discover molecular features and drivers of prostate cancer; (2) to develop and validate biomarkers and models to predict outcomes in men with prostate cancer; and (3) to develop clinical interventions to improve outcomes for men with prostate cancer.

title: Mechanisms of hematopoietic stem cell engraftment
text:
Haploidentical transplantation, where donors are matched at half of the HLA loci is a lifesaving alternative
for patients without a suitable donor, and who can only be cured by a hematopoietic stem cell transplantation.
Despite significant improvements, this curative treatment is still limited by increased rejection, often requiring
high-dose immunosuppression to sustain donor grafts. This proposal seeks to illuminate the mechanisms by
which the innate immune system recognizes haploidentical cells as foreign, with the ultimate goal to generate
novel therapies that will enhance the efficiency of allogeneic transplantation.

title: Multiple X-ray Source Array (MXA) Computed Tomography
text:
Multiple-X-ray Source Array-based ComputedTomography (MXA-CT)
Narrative
We propose the development of a brand-new type of x-ray tube which uses six or more sources
of radiation (sometimes simultaneously), and to use this new x-ray source to develop a faster
computed tomography scanner with much better image quality than existing systems. The multi
x-ray source array (MXA) is likely to revolutionize CT imaging, for standard whole body CT
systems and so-called cone beam CT systems which are specially built for dental, knee, breast,
and other imaging applications.

title: Development of multinuclear MRI for image guided therapy of glioma patients
text:
8. Project Narrative
The proposed research is relevant to public health because it will greatly improve the performance of MRI
scanners to image metabolic alterations in primary brain tumors. The new imaging methods will be used to
guide intra-operatively surgical resection of brain tumors and monitor treatment response. This will enable
precision oncology with targeted therapy tailored to the individual patient. Hence, this research is relevant to
NCI’s mission to advance diagnosis and treatment of cancer.

title: Explaining the potential role of physical activity in employment disparities after breast cancer
text: Breast cancer survivors are the largest group of cancer survivors and are at high risk for unemployment, potentially leading to financial toxicity and poor health outcomes. Despite the numerous benefits of employment for cancer survivors, cancer-related fatigue and cognitive impairment are common obstacles to working; these obstacles can be alleviated with physical activity, but accessibility to exercise opportunities and different experiences among those with limited education and lower income can adversely impact these outcomes. This study proposes an innovative approach to explore the relationship between physical activity and employment, and the impact of fatigue, cognitive impairment, accessibility to exercise opportunities, and different experiences based on education and income, gaining preliminary information to develop a future intervention targeting physical activity and work-life obstacles in breast cancer survivors susceptible to unemployment and physical inactivity.
